operator: Los Angeles Department of Animal Services
eligibility:
You must be 18 or older and live in the City of Los Angeles. Residents of Los Angeles County who live outside the city limits do not qualify. The animal has to be your own companion dog, cat, or rabbit. Stray, feral, and community cats, and animals tied to a rescue group, are excluded.

Each household can receive three certificates or coupons per species. A dog over four months old must be licensed before you request help for that dog. The application page links the city license form.
cost: Discount coupon, open to any eligible resident: up to $30–$50 toward sterilization. Free certificate, if your combined household income is below HUD's low-income limit: the full cost at a participating veterinary hospital or a clinic at a city shelter.
notice: On October 10, 2026 the application page said all 725 vouchers for that week were already taken. A new allotment is released Sundays at 10:00 AM. Check the application page before you apply.

operator: ASPCA Community Medicine, with surgery costs for income-qualifying residents reimbursed by the NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
eligibility:
Clinics serve limited zip codes, and the list changes with the calendar. On October 10, 2026 the ASPCA page listed: Brooklyn 11209, 11214, 11220, 11228, 11232; Bronx 10458, 10463, 10467, 10468, 10471; Manhattan 10032, 10033, 10034, 10040; Queens 11354, 11355, 11356, 11357, 11358, 11359, 11365, 11366, 11367; Staten Island 10302, 10303, 10310.

Bring photo ID showing you are 18 or older, and proof of a New York City address. The waitlist opens at 6:00 AM on the morning of the clinic and allows up to two pets. Signing up does not hold a spot. Go only after you receive a confirmation text. There are no walk-ins.
cost: Free with proof of one of these: NYCHA, Medicaid, SSI, SSDI, welfare, TANF, SNAP, or WIC. Without that proof, surgery is $125. Rabies and core vaccines, a nail trim, and a microchip are included only for animals having surgery that day.
notice: Zip codes and clinic dates change. Read the ASPCA page for the next date before you plan a trip. The city health department also lists this program at nyc.gov.

operator: Cook County Department of Animal and Rabies Control
eligibility:
You must live in Cook County, which includes Chicago. There is no coupon. Confirm that your veterinarian participates, then book the surgery in February. There is no household limit on the number of dogs and cats.

The pet needs a current rabies vaccine and a current Cook County rabies tag. Vaccination on the day of surgery is allowed.
cost: $40 off each dog or cat. If the clinic charges less than $40, the discount is $20. If the clinic charges less than $20, there is no discount. The program runs in February only.
notice: February 2026 has already ended. The next discount month is February 2027. The phone number is the department main line, from the agency page checked the same day.

operator: Fix.Adopt.Save. Maricopa County Animal Care and Control does not alter owned pets and refers people here.
eligibility:
You must live in Maricopa County, and the ID you bring to the appointment has to show that. The program is for owned pets of people who need help paying. It is not for breeders, sellers, shelters, rescues, fosters, animals being rehomed, or stray and community cats. Pets adopted from a shelter or rescue are also excluded; that organization is expected to handle sterilization.

The standing limit is 2 pets per household in a 12-month period. A whole litter, including the mother, can be an exception if you tell the clinic when you book. Assistance is not guaranteed and depends on grant funding.
cost: No copay is posted. When a voucher is issued, surgery is done by a participating veterinarian named on the voucher. Vouchers are mailed, not emailed. They are non-transferable, and an unused voucher is not extended or replaced.
notice: The public guidelines page says the request form is linked from that page. A separate form address was not published in the page text on October 10, 2026, so this link goes to the guidelines rather than a guessed form.

eligibility:
You must live in San Diego County or Imperial County. Households with income under $100,000 a year are given priority. Submitting the campus form requests an appointment. It is not confirmed until the Humane Society emails you.

Appointments are added every Tuesday after 12:00 PM for the following two weeks, except major holidays. Cancel at least 48 hours ahead.
cost: $230 to spay a female dog, $220 to neuter a male dog, $175 to spay a female cat, and $165 to neuter a male cat. A $75 deposit is not refunded if you cancel late or miss the appointment. Cryptorchid and brachycephalic pets can cost more; those fees are on the source page.
notice: The City of San Diego stopped funding its spay/neuter voucher at the end of June 2025. These are Humane Society clinic fees, not a city voucher. The San Diego campus clinic at 5500 Gaines Street is closed for October 2026. El Cajon, Escondido, and Oceanside are still listed.
